summary: Backend-only verification of the currency-propagation + AI-groundedness fix. New suite /app/backend/tests/test_currency_grounding.py (16 cases, 5 classes) run twice back-to-back: 16/16 PASS both runs. Covered: (1) fresh user -> onboarding with currency=USD -> POST /api/imports/csv with an all-INR CSV returns {currency:'INR', imported_records:9, generated_signals:3} and flips workspaces.currency to INR; (2) GET /api/overview -> workspace.currency=INR, data_source=csv, every money KPI value_display + supporting_amount + every feed[].amount_display uses the rupee sign, and a recursive walk of EVERY *_display key in the payload finds zero '$'; (3) GET /api/signals -> impact_display and every evidence[].amount_display in rupee, zero '$' anywhere, duplicate title is 'Potential duplicate payment — Cloud Vendor' / '— Ad Network India' (old 'Duplicate payment to' wording gone) and impact_amount is the single-payment excess (46000 / 27500, never 92000 / 55000); (4) GET /api/reports/executive -> workspace.currency, headline.revenue_recovered_display, open_pipeline_display, category_totals[].open_impact_display, top_actions[].impact_display, top_counterparties.customers[].invoiced_display and vendors[].spend_display all rupee, recursive *_display scan clean; (5) POST /api/ai/ask 'largest high-confidence finding' -> answer contains rupee, zero '$', no ungrounded phrase, contains grounding wording, citations non-empty with rupee amount_display; (6) POST /api/ai/ask 'How much has this business previously recovered?' -> answers 'No prior recovery amount is available in the current dataset.' with no fabricated figure; (7) SSE GET /api/ai/ask/stream -> event:open, multiple delta events, done payload text rupee-only with resolved rupee citations; (8) POST /api/signals/enrich -> LLM-rewritten explanations/recommended_actions contain no '$' and no ungrounded wording; (9) EDGE: CSV with no currency column falls back to USD even when onboarding said INR, mixed EUR/USD CSV picks the dominant EUR, onboarding currency=GBP with demo data renders in pounds; (10) REGRESSION: cfo@demo.seekprofit.app still USD on /overview, /signals and /reports (no rupee anywhere), /api/auth/me, /api/workspace/me, /api/signals/members, /signals/{id}/assign, /signals/{id}/status all 200, owner_email/due_date/sla_status still on the list. Demo workspace restored (15 signals, all open, no owners). No 5xx in backend logs during the run. No functional defect found for this iteration's fix; only groundedness-adjacent code-review observations below.

minor.issue: The brief is leaked verbatim into CFO-facing prose. Answers repeatedly say things like 'The brief explicitly marks prior_recovery_available as false' and 'which the brief classifies as a baseline-retained amount'. Internal JSON field names should never surface; add a style rule: never mention 'the brief' or its field names, phrase it as 'the current dataset contains no recovery history'.

Groundedness gap that survives this fix: compute_kpis() still sets revenue_recovered = 12% of paid invoices as a hardcoded heuristic and labels it amount_type='measured'. For the fresh INR CSV (zero resolved signals) Overview headlines 'Revenue Recovered ₹40.8K' — an invented figure, which is exactly the class of bug reported. dataset_facts.prior_recovery_available is correctly false, so the LLM receives contradictory inputs (it handled it well: '₹0 formally recovered to date, ₹40,800 retained as baseline'), but the UI KPI is still fabricated. Either drop the 12% baseline or relabel the card 'Retained revenue (baseline estimate)'.

_brief_for_ask puts the raw compute_kpis() dict into the brief with bare floats and NO *_display strings, so KPI amounts are the only numbers the LLM must format itself — the single remaining path where a '$' could slip in. Add value_display (currency-formatted) to the kpis block in the brief for symmetry with top_signals/sample_records.

Docstrings and comments still talk in '$' terms ('cumulative $ of resolved signals', '20 % of paid invoices', '$250k -> ~0.9') and priority_score buckets impact by a fixed 10,000 unit. For INR/JPY workspaces the log-impact bucketing is currency-blind, so priority scores are not comparable across currencies (₹46,000 scores like $46,000). Not user-visible now, but worth a note.

action_items: Prompt polish: forbid the model from referencing 'the brief' or internal field names (prior_recovery_available, dataset_facts) in answers.

Decide on the 12%-of-paid-invoices 'Revenue Recovered' KPI — it is a fabricated 'measured' number and contradicts dataset_facts.prior_recovery_available=false. Rename the card or gate it behind resolved signals.
Add currency-formatted *_display fields to the kpis block inside _brief_for_ask so the LLM never has to format a raw number itself.

(Carried over, unfixed from iteration 3) Push signal ordering into the Mongo query; zero-fill all three category_totals buckets; accept the Bearer header on /api/ai/ask/stream instead of ?token=; ActionCenterPage React key warning + 390px horizontal overflow.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/imports.py: the dominant-currency vote is computed over rows AFTER _parse_csv already defaulted blank currency cells to 'USD'. A CSV that is 60% INR rows and 40% blank cells still resolves to INR, but a 45/55 split silently flips the whole workspace to USD. Count only rows that actually declared a currency, then fall back to USD when none did.

routers/imports.py: currency is written to the workspace but the per-record 'currency' field is kept, and nothing rejects a genuinely mixed-currency CSV. Amounts in different currencies are summed together in compute_kpis/detectors (verified: the mixed EUR/USD CSV totals EUR and USD amounts into one EUR figure). At minimum return a warning in the import response when >1 distinct currency is present.

The workspace lookup helper (_wid / _wid_and_currency / _workspace) is now duplicated in 6 routers and each re-derives ws.get('currency','USD') — still not extracted into a shared dependency as flagged in iteration 3; every new endpoint is one more place to forget the currency.

services/finance.py format_currency abbreviates at >=1000 with K/M using Western grouping. For INR the culturally expected grouping is lakh/crore (₹1.10M reads oddly for ₹11,00,000). Consider locale-aware abbreviation, or at least keep exact formatting for INR.
CURRENCY_SYMBOLS maps CAD/AUD/SGD to a bare '$', so a CAD workspace renders identically to USD and any test asserting 'no $' would false-positive. Prefer 'CA$'/'A$'/'S$'.
seed_data_creation: Throwaway registrations only: curr_qa_*/curr_ai_*/curr_edge_*/probe_*@seekprofit.app (password testpass123), each with its own workspace and CSV-imported records. Demo workspace cfo@demo.seekprofit.app was only read plus one assign/status/unassign cycle that was reverted — verified end state 15 signals, all open, no owners, currency USD.
test_credentials: cfo@demo.seekprofit.app / demo1234 (USD workspace, intact). INR workspaces are created on the fly by the suite.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_currency_grounding.py -v (about 27s; pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope, do not edit). Gotchas learned: (1) Overview KPI objects use 'slug', not 'key', and the two count KPIs ('leaks','actions') have no currency symbol in value_display — skip them when asserting on symbols, but DO assert on their supporting_amount; (2) do not blanket-match forbidden phrases like 'confirmed duplicate' in AI answers — the model legitimately writes 'these are high-confidence findings requiring review, not confirmed duplicates'; use the ungrounded_phrases() helper in the suite which ignores negated occurrences (this caused the only failure of the run and was a test bug, not a product bug); (3) /api/imports/csv needs multipart, so build a separate requests.Session without the JSON Content-Type header; (4) the CSV import wipes financial_records + signals for the workspace, so give every currency scenario its own fresh user. Not covered this iteration: any frontend/Playwright checks (explicitly skipped), JPY/zero-decimal formatting, and a mixed-currency CSV rejection path (none exists).
rca_of_the_issue: Original defect root cause confirmed fixed at the source: /api/imports/csv now votes on the dominant CSV currency and persists it to workspaces.currency, and every serializer (overview._format_kpis, signals._serialize, reports._category_totals/_top_counterparties, ai._resolve_citations) threads that value into finance.format_currency/format_amount_exact instead of a hardcoded '$'. Groundedness is enforced two ways: build_system_prompt() bans invented figures/history and the 'confirmed' vocabulary, and _brief_for_ask() ships dataset_facts.prior_recovery_available so the model has a deterministic fact to fall back on — observed answers now open with 'No prior recovery amount is available in the current dataset.' Duplicate impact is amount * (len(cluster)-1) in detectors.py, i.e. the excess only, verified as 27500/46000 for two-payment clusters.
